Rashi on Sukkah 2a:10:1.hebrew: עשתרות קרנים - שני הרים גדולים והשפלה ביניהם, ומתוך גובה ההרים אין חמה זורחת שם בשפלה:
Rashi on Sukkah 2a:10:1.english: Ashterot Karnayim - [These were] two large mountains and the lowland between them, and due to the height of the mountains, the sun does not shine there in the lowland.

Rashi on Sukkah 2a:11:1.hebrew: דל דפנות ליכא צל סוכה - שחמה באה מתחתי', נמצא שמה בטל:
Rashi on Sukkah 2a:11:1.english: [If you] remove the walls, there is no shade of a sukkah - For the sun comes in from underneath it, [and] thus its name [as a sukkah] is nullified.

Rashi on Sukkah 2a:12:1.hebrew: שבעת ימים - סוכה של שבעה ותו לא, דהיינו עראי, ודייה במחיצות קלות:
Rashi on Sukkah 2a:12:1.english: Seven days - A sukkah for seven [days] and no more, which is temporary, and light partitions suffice for it.

Rashi on Sukkah 2a:12:2.hebrew: למעלה מעשרים - צריך לעשות יסודותיה ומחיצותיה קבועין, שלא תפול:
Rashi on Sukkah 2a:12:2.english: Above twenty [cubits] - One must make its foundations and its walls permanent, so that it will not fall.

Rashi on Sukkah 2a:14:1.hebrew: עד עשרים אמה דאדם עושה כו' - שפיר דמי, דודאי יש בכלל קבע עראי, והרי עשה כתורה. ועל כרחך לא הקפידה תורה על העראי אלא לשם שיעור, לתת לך שיעור בגובהה, שתהא יכולה לעמוד על ידי יתידות עראי:
Rashi on Sukkah 2a:14:1.english: Up to twenty cubits, where a person makes, etc. - It is acceptable, for certainly a temporary [dwelling] is included within a permanent [dwelling], and behold, he has acted in accordance with the Torah. And perforce, the Torah was not particular about [the dwelling being] temporary except for the purpose of a measurement — to give you a measurement for its height, [such] that it is capable of standing by means of temporary pegs.

Rashi on Sukkah 2a:1:1.english: A sukkah... and Rabbi Yehuda deems it fit - In the Gemara, it explains their dispute.

Rashi on Sukkah 2a:2:1.english: And [one] that is not ten [handbreadths] high - In the Gemara, it explains the reason.

Rashi on Sukkah 2a:2:2.english: Three walls - [The Gemara] also derives them in the Gemara.

Rashi on Sukkah 2a:2:3.hebrew: ושחמתה מרובה מצלתה - המועט בטל ברוב, והרי הוא כמי שאינו, ועל שם הסכך קרויה סוכה:
Rashi on Sukkah 2a:2:3.english: And [one] whose sunlight is greater than its shade - The minority is nullified in the majority, and it is as though it does not exist; and it is called a sukkah after the sekhakh [covering].

Rashi on Sukkah 2a:3:1.hebrew: מבוי שהוא גבוה - מבוי שהוא סתום משלש צדדין, וראשו פתוח לרשות הרבים, וחצירות פתוחות לו ויוצאות ובאות לרשות הרבים — הרי הוא רשות היחיד לבני חצירות. ואסרו חכמים להוציא מרשותו לרשות חבירו בלא עירוב, שהחצירות כל אחת רשות לעצמה, והמבוי רשות לכולן. והצריכו בו שיתוף, להשתתף כל החצירות בפת או ביין, ולהניח השיתוף באחת מן החצירות. ולפי שאין לו מחיצה רביעית, וקרוב הוא להיות דומה לרשות הרבים, הצריכו היכר בראשו הפתוח לרשות הרבים — או לחי זקוף, או קורה מכותל לכותל. ואם גבוה הקורה מעשרים אמה:
Rashi on Sukkah 2a:3:1.english: An alleyway that is higher - An alleyway that is enclosed on three sides and its end opens into the public domain, and courtyards open into it and [their residents] go out and come in to the public domain [through it] — it is a private domain for the residents of the courtyards. And the Sages prohibited carrying out from one's domain into another's domain without an eruv, for each courtyard is a domain in its own right, and the alleyway is a domain common to all of them. And they required a shittuf [partnership] for it, that all the courtyards join together in bread or in wine, and place the shittuf in one of the courtyards. And because it does not have a fourth partition and is close to resembling a public domain, they required a recognizable marker at its end that opens into the public domain — either an upright post or a crossbeam from wall to wall. And if the beam is higher than twenty cubits [one must diminish it].

Rashi on Sukkah 2a:3:2.english: He must reduce - He must lower [it].

Rashi on Sukkah 2a:3:3.english: He does not need to - And there [in tractate Eruvin], the reason is explained.

Rashi on Sukkah 2a:5:1.hebrew: סוכה מדאורייתא - דעשרים אמה דילה ילפינן מדאורייתא, וקודם שנשנית המשנה נאמרה שיעורה מסיני:
Rashi on Sukkah 2a:5:1.english: A sukkah [is] from the Torah - For its [limit of] twenty cubits we derive from the Torah, and before the Mishnah was taught, its measure was stated from Sinai.

Rashi on Sukkah 2a:5:2.hebrew: תני פסולה - שייך למיתני בה לשון פסול, כלומר: לא נעשית כתורה וכהלכה:
Rashi on Sukkah 2a:5:2.english: [The Tanna] teaches "it is invalid" - It is appropriate to teach regarding it the language of invalidity, that is to say: it was not made in accordance with the Torah and the Halakhah.

Rashi on Sukkah 2a:5:3.hebrew: מבוי - דכוליה מדרבנן, דמדאורייתא סגי ליה בשלש מחיצות, ואינו צריך לקורה זו אלא מדרבנן:
Rashi on Sukkah 2a:5:3.english: An alleyway - For it is entirely Rabbinic, as by Torah law three partitions suffice for it, and it does not require this crossbeam except Rabbinically.

Rashi on Sukkah 2a:5:4.hebrew: תני תקנתא - דלא שייך למתני בה לשון פסול, דמאן פסלה קודם שנשנית משנה זו? הרי היא תחלת הוראתו ומצותו:
Rashi on Sukkah 2a:5:4.english: [It] teaches a remedy - For it is not appropriate to teach regarding it the term 'invalid,' for who invalidated it before this Mishnah was taught? Behold, this [Mishnah] is the beginning of its instruction and its commandment.

Rashi on Sukkah 2a:6:1.english: And if you wish, say: Regarding Torah [law] as well - It is applicable to state a remedy.

Rashi on Sukkah 2a:6:2.hebrew: סוכה דנפישי מילתה - ואין דומין תקנותיהן זו לזו, וצריך לשנות הלשון לכל תקנה ותקנה — כגון: בגבוהה ימעט, וכשאינה גבוהה יגביה, ושאין לה שלש דפנות יעשה לה, ושחמתה מרובה יוסיף סכך. הלכך, פסיק ותני פסולה, דמצי למיכללינהו לכולהו בהך פסולה; דקיימא לן (פסחים דף ג:), ישנה אדם לתלמידו דרך קצרה:
Rashi on Sukkah 2a:6:2.english: A sukka, whose matters are numerous - And their remedies are not similar to one another, and [the tanna] would need to vary the wording for each and every remedy — such as: for a tall [sukka], "he must lower [it]"; and when it is not tall [enough], "he must raise [it]"; and for one that does not have three walls, "he must make [walls] for it"; and for one whose sunlight is greater [than its shade], "he must add sekhakh." Therefore, [the tanna] categorically teaches "it is invalid," since he can include all of them in this [term] "it is invalid"; for we maintain (Pesachim 3b): "A person should teach his student in a concise manner."

Rashi on Sukkah 2a:6:3.english: An alleyway, its matters are not numerous - In that mishna.

Rashi on Sukkah 2a:8:1.hebrew: למען ידעו - עשה סוכה שישיבתה ניכרת לך, דכתיב: "ידעו כי בסוכות הושבתי" — צויתי לישב, הכי דריש ליה. ואע"ג דאין יוצא מידי פשוטו — דהיקף ענני כבוד — מיהו דרשינן ליה לדרשה:
Rashi on Sukkah 2a:8:1.english: So that [your generations] will know - Make a sukkah such that dwelling in it is noticeable to you, for it is written: “[so that] they shall know that in sukkot I caused [them] to dwell” — [meaning,] I commanded [them] to dwell; this is how he expounds it. And even though [the verse] does not depart from its plain meaning — [which refers to] the surrounding of the clouds of glory — nevertheless, we expound it for a homiletical derivation.

Rashi on Sukkah 2a:8:2.hebrew: דלא שלטא בה עינא - שאינו רואה את הסכך, וסוכה היינו סכך, כשמה:
Rashi on Sukkah 2a:8:2.english: That the eye does not reach it - [Meaning] that one does not see the roofing; and a sukkah is [essentially] the roofing [sekhakh], as its name [indicates].

Rashi on Sukkah 2a:9:1.english: And there shall be a sukkah for shade - This implies that sekhakh is only that which is made for shade.

Rashi on Sukkah 2a:9:2.hebrew: אלא בצל דפנות - שהצללין מגיעין זה לזה מתוך גובהן של דפנות, ואין צריך סכך. ולקמן מוקי פלוגתייהו לר' זירא בשאין בה אלא ארבע על ארבע, דקים להו לרבנן דבהאי שיעורא ליכא צל סכך אלא צל של דפנות:
Rashi on Sukkah 2a:9:2.english: Rather, in the shade of the walls - For the shadows reach one another due to the height of the walls, and roofing is not needed [to provide shade]. And later [in the Gemara], it establishes their dispute according to Rabbi Zeira [as referring to a case] where it has only four [cubits] by four [cubits], for the Sages are certain that with this measurement, there is no shade of the roofing, but rather [only] the shade of the walls.

Tosafot on Sukkah 2a:14:1.hebrew: כי עביד ליה דירת קבע שפיר דמי - דאע"ג דיש לפרש קרא בדירה שאינה ראויה אלא לשבעה, למעוטי קבע — משמע ליה קרא דאתא לשיעורא, לאורויי לך מדת גובהה; כלו', בסוכה שאפשר לעשות עראי. וא"ת: וכיון דלא חיישינן אלא שתהא ראויה לעשותה עראי, ואע"פ שעושה אותה קבע, א"כ אמאי אמר (תענית דף ב.) "גשמים סימן קללה בחג"? והלא יכול לקבוע הנסרים במסמרים, שלא ירדו גשמים בסוכה? ואפילו תימצי לומר דאסור משום גזרת תקרה, כי היכי דאמר לקמן בפירקין (סוכה דף יד.) גבי פלוגתא דר"מ ורבי יהודה דמסככין בנסרין, דאי מכשרת בהו אתי למימר: "מה לי לסכך בזה, מה לי לישב תחת תקרת ביתי", וביתו ודאי פסול מדאורייתא, ד"סוכה" אמר רחמנא ולא ביתו של כל ימות השנה — מ"מ, כיון דלא אסור אלא מדרבנן, לא שייכא למימר שהגשמים סימן קללה! וי"ל: דנהי דלא חיישינן בדפנות אי עביד להו קבע, מ"מ בסככה, שעיקר הסוכה על שם הסכך, לא מיתכשרה עד דעביד לה עראי. ומה"ט נמי ניחא לרבי זירא, דדריש מדכתי' "וסוכה תהיה לצל" — הא כתי' נמי "מזרם וממטר", וניבעי נמי שלא ירדו גשמים לתוכה? אלא ודאי, משום דבעינן סככה עראי, וא"כ הוה ליה קבע:
Tosafot on Sukkah 2a:14:1.english: "When he makes it a permanent dwelling, it is acceptable" - For even though the verse could be interpreted as [referring to] a dwelling that is suitable only for seven [days], [thus] excluding a permanent [dwelling], the verse indicates to [Rava] that it comes to [teach] a measurement, to instruct you regarding the measure of its height — that is to say, [it applies] to a sukkah that is possible to make temporary. And if you say: Since we are concerned only that it be suitable to be made temporary, even though he [in fact] makes it permanent, if so, why did [the Mishnah] say (Ta'anit 2a): "Rain is a sign of a curse on the Festival"? For could he not fix the planks with nails so that rain would not fall into the sukkah? And even if you should say that it is forbidden due to the rabbinic decree of a ceiling, just as [the Gemara] says later in our chapter (Sukkah 14a) regarding the dispute of Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehudah concerning covering [a sukkah] with planks — that if you validate them, one will come to say: "What is the difference to me whether I cover [the sukkah] with this, or whether I sit beneath the ceiling of my house?" And one's house is certainly invalid by Torah law, as the Merciful One stated "a sukkah" and not his year-round house — nevertheless, since it is forbidden only rabbinically, it is not applicable to say that rain is a sign of a curse! And one can say: Granted that we are not concerned regarding the walls if he makes them permanent; nevertheless, regarding its roofing [sekhakh] — since the essence of the sukkah is [named] for the sekhakh — it is not valid until he makes it temporary. And for this reason as well, it works out well according to Rabbi Zeira, who derives [his view] from that which is written: "And there shall be a sukkah for shade in the daytime" (Isaiah 4:6) — behold, it is also written: "from storm and from rain"! And shouldn't we also require that rain not fall into it? Rather, it is certainly because we require that its roofing be temporary, and if so [if it kept out the rain], it would be permanent.

Tosafot on Sukkah 2a:4:1.hebrew: מאי שנא גבי סוכה דתני פסולה ומאי שנא גבי מבוי דתני תקנתא - והא דלא פריך: "מאי שנא גבי הדס דתני פסולה ותקנתא", דתנן בפרק לולב הגזול (לקמן סוכה דף לב:): "או שהיו ענביו מרובין מעליו פסול, ואם מיעטן כשר" — דלא פריך אלא מסוכה ומבוי, שדינם שוה לענין גבוה ושינה לשון משנתו. ועוד, דגבי הדס אצטריך למיתני תקנתא, דס"ד אמינא: כיון דגדולו בפסול — תו לית ליה תקנתא:
Tosafot on Sukkah 2a:4:1.english: "What is different regarding a sukkah that it teaches [that it is] invalid, and what is different regarding an alleyway that it teaches [its] rectification?" - And as for that which [the Gemara] does not ask: "What is different regarding a myrtle branch (hadas) that [the Mishnah] teaches [both] invalidation and rectification?" — as we learned in the chapter "Lulav HaGazul" (below, Sukkah 32b): "Or if its berries were more numerous than its leaves, it is invalid; and if he diminished them, it is valid" — [the reason is] that [the Gemara] only objected from [the cases of] a sukkah and an alleyway, whose law is identical regarding height, yet [the Tanna] changed the phrasing of his Mishnah. And furthermore, regarding the myrtle branch it was necessary [for the Mishnah] to teach the rectification, for it might enter your mind to say: Since its growth was in [a state of] invalidity, it no longer has any rectification.

Tosafot on Sukkah 2a:5:1.hebrew: דאורייתא תני פסולה - דאי הוה תני ימעט, חיישינן דילמא טעי איניש לומר: "ימעט לכתחילה, ודיעבד כשרה". ודקדק בלשונו דלמא אתי לידי איסורא דאורייתא, ותני פסולה, אע"ג דלא הוי לישנא מעליא כמו ימעט. אבל במבוי, דרבנן, לא חייש, ותנא ימעט, שהוא לישנא מעליא — כדאשכחן בריש פסחים (דף ג.): שעקם הכתוב כמה אותיות שלא להוציא דבר מגונה מפיו. ובקונטרס לא פירש כן. אי נמי, יש לומר: דלשון ימעט משמע חומרא דרבנן בעלמא, ופסולה משמע דאורייתא. ובפרק במה מדליקין (שבת דף כב.) דאמרינן: "נר חנוכה שהניחה למעלה מעשרים אמה פסולה כסוכה וכמבוי" — אגב דתנן כסוכה, נקט נמי גבי נר חנוכה פסולה. א"נ, אי הוה תני ימעט, הוה משמע: כמות שהיתה מדלקת ישפילנה; וזה אינו למאן דאמר הדלקה עושה מצוה. ואפי' למ"ד הנחה עושה מצוה, חיישינן דהרואה אומר: "לצורכו הוא מדליקה", כדאמרינן גבי הדליקה בפנים והניחה בחוץ:
Tosafot on Sukkah 2a:5:1.english: "[Since a sukkah is] by Torah law, [the tanna] teaches 'it is invalid'" - For had he taught "he must lower it" [as he did regarding an alleyway], we would be concerned lest a person err to say: "He must lower it ab initio, but post facto [if he did not lower it] it is valid." Therefore, [the tanna] was meticulous in his phrasing lest [people] come to a biblical violation, and taught "it is invalid," even though it is not as refined an expression as "he must lower it." But regarding an alleyway, which is rabbinic, he was not concerned [about such an error], and taught "he must lower it," which is a more refined expression — as we find at the beginning of Pesachim (3a): Scripture used a circumlocution of several letters in order not to utter an unseemly word from its mouth. And in the Kunteres [Rashi], he did not explain [it] this way. Alternatively, it can be said: The phrasing "he must lower it" implies merely a rabbinic stringency, whereas "it is invalid" implies [an invalidation] by Torah law. And regarding that which we say in the chapter Bameh Madlikin (Shabbat 22a): "A Hanukkah lamp that one placed above twenty cubits is invalid, like a sukkah and like an alleyway" — since it stated "like a sukkah," it also employed "it is invalid" regarding the Hanukkah lamp. Alternatively, had it taught "he must lower it," it would have implied that while it was burning he should lower it; and this is not so according to the one who holds that kindling accomplishes the mitzvah. And even according to the one who holds that placement accomplishes the mitzvah, we are concerned that an onlooker will say: "He is lighting it for his own needs," as we say regarding [one who] kindled it inside and placed it outside.

Tosafot on Sukkah 2a:8:1.hebrew: אמר רבה אמר קרא למען ידעו כו' - קצת קשה ללישנא קמא דבריש עירובין (דף ג.), גבי מקצת סוכה בתוך עשרים, דאמר רבה: "הסוכה פסולה" — הא שלטה בה עינא, כיון דאין חללה עשרים! ורבה גרס התם כי הכא, דהא רבא פליג התם ואמר: "זה וזה כשר, חלל סוכה תנן, חלל מבוי תנן". ויש לומר: דהא מפרש התם טעמא, משום דסוכה דביחיד קא הוי', לא קא מדכר, וזימנין דמישתקיל מלתחת עובי הסכך הנכנס לתוך עשרים, וקיימא כולה למעלה מעשרים. ורבינא נמי דמשני: "סוכה דאורייתא, אחמירו בה רבנן" — מ"מ משמע דמדאורייתא כשרה:
Tosafot on Sukkah 2a:8:1.english: Rabbah said: The verse states, "So that your generations may know," etc. - [This is] somewhat difficult according to the first version at the beginning of Eruvin (3a) regarding [the case where] part of the sukkah is within twenty [cubits], where Rabbah said: "The sukkah is unfit" — for doesn't the eye discern it, since its interior space is not twenty [cubits high]? And the reading there is Rabbah [with a heh], just as here, for Rava [with an alef] disagrees there and said: "Both this and that are fit; we learned [in the mishna regarding] the airspace of the sukkah, we learned [regarding] the airspace of the alleyway." And one can say: for [the Gemara] indeed explains the reason there: because a sukkah is [used] by an individual, he will not be reminded, and at times the thickness of the roofing that enters within the twenty [cubits] might be removed from below, and it will entirely stand above twenty [cubits]. And Ravina too, who answers: "A sukkah is [a mitzvah] from the Torah, [so] the Rabbis were stringent regarding it" — nevertheless, it implies that by Torah law it is fit.
